title: Introduction to CSS
description: Get started with the basics of CSS, its purpose, syntax, and how it integrates with HTML to style web pages.

lessons.title: What is CSS?
lessons.content: CSS (Cascading Style Sheets) is used to style and layout HTML elements. It controls colors, fonts, spacing, positioning, and responsiveness across the web.

lessons.title: Why Use CSS?
lessons.content: CSS separates content from design, improves website maintainability, reduces code duplication, and allows consistent styling across multiple pages.

lessons.title: Ways to Apply CSS: Inline, Internal, External
lessons.content: CSS can be applied in three ways: inline (within HTML tags), internal (inside a <style> tag), and external (linked CSS file). External CSS is best for scalability.

lessons.title: Basic CSS Syntax
CSS Selectors: Element, Class, ID
How to Link a CSS File to HTML
lessons.content:
<!-- Inside the <head> of your HTML document -->
<link rel="stylesheet" href="styles.css">

lessons.title: CSS Comments and Best Practices
lessons.content: CSS comments use /* like this */. Use comments to organize styles logically. Keep selectors clean, avoid inline CSS, and use external stylesheets for large projects.

lessons.title: Applying Multiple Rules to One Element
Understanding Cascading and Specificity
lessons.content: When multiple rules target the same element, CSS decides which one applies based on specificity and order. IDs > Classes > Elements in specificity.

lessons.title: Inspecting Styles in the Browser
lessons.content: Right-click and choose 'Inspect' to open DevTools. Use the 'Elements' and 'Styles' panel to see how CSS is applied and debug your styles live.
